propositions: Four single-file AST guards scan hardcoded source files where policed constructs no longer reside after module splits, causing guards to pass unconditionally with zero occurrences of the scanned pattern.

Guards F1–F4 measure zero instances of their policed constructs in scanned targets: invariants imports in applier.py, timeout patterns in runner.py, rebar imports in inbound_probe.py, and string-split calls in usage_log.py.

Guards lacking anti-vacuity assertions become brittle to refactoring; proven by comparison with surviving guards test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py:630 and test_web_tool_gating.py:130 that assert scan population is non-empty.

Repair pattern: widen scan scope from single file to module transitive closure, replace filename pinning with population derivation, add landmark assertions requiring key constructs to exist in scanned modules, and verify with mutation tests.
Findings F5 and F7 require anti-vacuity assertions or explicit scope justification; F8 is a false positive (matched substrings in non-defective code).
